$comment: NIP-ME promotion-validator conformance fixtures — shared oracle for the engine-side typed promotion validator, in the NIP-MP.fixtures.json tradition: reject cases name the rule identifiers they must fire (see NIP-ME 'Validator rule identifiers') so an implementation cannot pass by rejecting for an unrelated reason. Unlike NIP-MP (unsigned relay-ingest templates), these cases evaluate a promotion DECISION: the validator receives the admitted kind:40200 proposal, the reviewer's kind:40203 verdict with its proof bundle, the promotion-granting NIP-SD v3 keyed proofs, and engine state (generation, admission time, frozen policy snapshot), and MUST produce exactly the `expect` outcome. Structure: `positive_control` is the one fully valid tuple; every other case is a stated mutation of it — most are a single field set, and where a case sets two fields the note says why. Apply a mutation by deep-copying the control (minus `name`/`expect`/`receipt_asserts`/`note`/`reject_rules`/`mutations`) and setting each `mutations[i].path` to `mutations[i].value`; dotted paths index arrays as `grants[0]`, and a value of the form `<actors.NAME>` resolves to that actor's pubkey from `actors`. `expect` values: reject (loud error naming one of `reject_rules`), no_promotion_authorized (fail-closed to human review across the whole grant set — authorizes nothing, not a single-event error), remains_review (no valid proof exists; the item never left review — not an error), promote (governed promotion event minted; receipt labels asserted). Spec: docs/nips/NIP-ME.md (Delegated review verdicts, Validator rule identifiers, Promotion policy and receipts); grant shapes: docs/nips/NIP-SD.md (v3 payload).

proposal.statement: edge runtime pins 4.2.1 after the 2026-09-01 upgrade

cases.name: promote_valid_delegated_verdict
cases.note: Positive control, applied verbatim: current generation, promoter != proposer, reviewer-owned post-admission evidence bound to the 40200 payload hash, valid v3 keyed grant, allowlist agreeing across both granting proofs. Receipt must carry authority=delegated_agent, verification_class=reproduced_by_promoter, reproducible_by=privileged.

cases.name: reject_copied_proof
cases.note: Evidence produced and signed by the proposer, pasted into the verdict. Producer-bound means the reviewer signs its own evidence after admission; proposer-supplied evidence is the laundering path.

cases.name: reject_proof_predates_admission
cases.note: Valid-looking reviewer evidence whose signature predates the proposal's admission time — it cannot have been produced for this item.

cases.name: reject_unbound_verifier
cases.note: The proof bundle's bound_verifier is another_reviewer while the verdict is signed by reviewer. The bundle must bind the promoting key itself.

cases.name: reject_stale_generation
cases.note: The approve was evaluated at generation 4102; the engine has since advanced to 4103 within the claim's dependency set. Reject to re-verification at head — never queue, never warn.

cases.name: reject_promoter_equals_proposer
cases.note: Two fields move as one identity swap (actor and bound_verifier both become the proposer) so that only promoter-not-proposer can fire: a validator that rejects this via bound-verifier-equals-promoter instead has not implemented the protocol MUST.

cases.name: reject_route_to_nobody
cases.note: Policy routes review but the resolved reviewer set is empty. Loud rejection at admission, never a void item nobody owns.

cases.name: reject_v3_aggregate_shape
cases.note: A proof carrying version:3 in the aggregate shape (per-capability subjects, no granteePubkey). Known version, unknown document — v3 exists only in the keyed singular shape (NIP-SD), so this fails validation loud, same as an unknown version.

cases.name: reject_memory_promotion_boolean_true
cases.note: memory_promotion granted as bare true. Granting without naming claim types is not a shape its author can have meant; fail loud, never interpret as unrestricted.

cases.name: reject_claim_type_outside_vocabulary
cases.note: claimTypes includes identity_mapping — outside the delegable vocabulary. Fail loud rather than narrowing to the known subset: a reader that silently ignored an unrecognized claim type would widen the grant.

cases.name: reject_empty_claim_types
cases.note: claimTypes is []. An empty grant is an authoring error, not a silent none.

cases.name: reject_allowlist_on_non_granting_proof
cases.note: humanFallbackAllowlist retained by a keyed proof whose memory_promotion is now false. The field exists only on granting proofs; this needs an explicit deny check, not serde defaults.

cases.name: no_promotion_disagreeing_allowlists
cases.note: Two keyed proofs both granting memory_promotion with differing humanFallbackAllowlist values (restored-backup / partial-write shape). Fail closed to human review: no promotion is authorized by any of them. Not a rejection — carries no rule identifier.

cases.name: remains_review_no_probe
cases.note: fact_proposal with no registered probe, so no valid proof exists. The item never leaves review — structural default, not an error and not an escalation requirement.
